collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Children revive an old stone game but change all the rules: let them, or teach the old rules.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) found the old stone game board carved into a rock by the shore, and have started playing it, with rules they made up. (third), who played it as a child, is horrified: they are moving the stones backwards. What should (third) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (third) watches, and tries not to say anything. The children's version is fast and loud and very silly. One afternoon, (third) asks to play. (third.He/she) loses badly, and laughs.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (third) teaches them the old rules. The children find it slow. Then they find the clever moves, and become obsessed. Within a month they beat (third), who is very proud.
